children.game_version: A 'statue' game where children move slowly and quietly while the music is lively, stopping when the daf stops.

seniors.seated_version: Perform the 'slow and quiet' arm and hand gestures while seated, focusing on the 6/8 rhythm.
seniors.standing_version: Gentle swaying in place to the 6/8 meter, avoiding complex footwork.
seniors.tempo_and_range: Reduce the range of arm movements to shoulder height.

social_formats.description: Performed at parties, weddings, and holidays by young women and girls.

movement_profile.tempo_feel: Moderately lively pace with slow and quiet motions
movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Avoid aggressive or rapid jerky movements; the sources emphasize 'slow and quiet' motions.

music_profile.sound_description: The sound is dominated by the plucked resonance of the tar and the melodic wail of the kamancha, underpinned by the steady, driving 6/8 beat of the daf frame drum.

basic_steps: Maintain a slow and quiet upper body posture
Step in time with the 6/8 rhythm
Coordinate hand movements with the moderately lively pace of the tar
teaching.level_notes: The dance requires a balance between slow, graceful arm movements and a moderately fast musical tempo.
